objective_for_doctor: A 62-year-old M patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: diarrhea.

I’ve had diarrhea or an increase in stool frequency. I also feel nauseous or like vomiting, and I’m very tired—I’m unable to do my usual activities or I’m stuck in my bed all day long.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—how long has the diarrhea been going on, and is there any blood or black/tarry stool?  
Doctor: Do you have fever, severe belly pain, or recent travel/food poisoning, and are you on any new medications (especially antibiotics, metformin, or laxatives)?

I’ve had diarrhea or an increase in stool frequency. I also have a fever (felt or measured). I’ve also traveled out of the country to West Africa in the last 4 weeks.

I don’t know about blood or black/tarry stool, severe belly pain, or new medications (including antibiotics, metformin, or laxatives).

Doctor: Given your fever and travel to West Africa within 4 weeks, I’m concerned about an infectious cause—are you having severe watery diarrhea (how many times/day), any vomiting, and are you able to keep fluids down or are you getting dizzy/very thirsty?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Stool_Culture_and_ova_parasite (including Giardia/Cryptosporidium), plus Rapid_PCR_panel if available  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: CBC, CMP (electrolytes/creatinine), and stool test for C_difficile if any recent antibiotics occurred
